pages.title: File:Medieval jetton (FindID 825658).jpg

ObjectName.value: Medieval jetton

Artist.value: Derby Museums Trust, Alastair Willis, 2017-04-19 15:32:10

ImageDescription.value:
A copper alloy medieval French jetton probably dating from the reign of Louis II, Count of Flanders (1346-1384). The obverse is very worn but depicts a rampant lion on a shield within a tressure of 6 arches. The reverse shows a central lis within a bowed cross flory, each terminal bearing a lis, and a lis in each quarter.

This jetton is very similar to <a href="https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/448646" title="View details for SUR-A21CC0">SUR-A21CC0</a> and <a href="https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/759097" title="View details for BH-2B6D64">BH-2B6D64</a>. Similar jettons are illustrated by Mitchiner (1988: 250-251); however, the legend on this jetton is unlisted. A likely reading is: (obverse) 'LES GETOVERS DE LA CH; (reverse) DE NEI/ORS/VLA', which probably translates as 'The jettons of the Chamber of Finance, Flanders'. The Chambre aux Deniers is alluded to by Mitchiner (ibid. 232), who states: '...[it] was financed by the Trèsor and was responsible for managing the expenditure of the offices comprising the Maison du Roi.'
